sesquĭplāris , is, and sesquĭplā-rĭus , ii, m. sesquiplex,
I.a soldier who received a ration and a half as a reward for his bravery, Veg. Mil. 2, 7; Inscr. Rein. cl. 8, n. 13; Inscr. Orell. 3476; called also SESQVIPLICARIVS, Hyg. Grom. med.; Inscr. Fabr. p. 104, n. 245; “and SESCVPLICARIVS,” Inscr. Orell. 3408 ; 3416.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
